log: THE DOCTRINE TURNED ON THE REST OF THE REPO
The rules are about METHOD, so they apply to a knockout predictor as much as to an
eigensolver. Evidence classes are kept apart and never summed:
GIT     strong -- the commit graph records what happened rather than claiming it
OUTPUT  medium -- a recorded run either contains a failing verdict or it does not
TEXT    WEAK   -- the word 'control' in a file proves the author knew the word
STRONG -- the commit graph. 'runs' is how many modules record a result at all.
subsystem                         mods  runs  cover  GIT gate
CIRCULAR -- these search for physics_reduce's own verdict words, so it scores 100%
by construction. Read as vocabulary ADOPTION, never as whether negatives get reported.
TEXT checks -- weak evidence, kept separate on purpose
THE CONTROL -- can this audit tell good practice from its absence?
prototype_p* was useless as a low set: 0 of 24 have a recorded output, so both
STRONG checks were not comparable. Using oldest vs newest third of everything that HAS a
recorded output instead -- 11 modules each, out of 33.
OUTPUT_has_negative             0% newest vs     0% oldest   does not separate
OUTPUT_has_graded               0% newest vs     9% oldest   does not separate
The audit separates the two calibration sets, so the per-subsystem numbers above
carry information. They still measure DECLARED practice, not correctness.
